1: //! # SYSTEM_OBJECTS_ENGINE: System Object Validation Checks
2: //!
3: //! Implements 9 checks for MATLAB System object validation. System objects
4: //! (classes inheriting from `matlab.System`) have specific lifecycle
5: //! constraints that static analysis can partially verify.
6: //!
7: //! Since full type information is not available to a static linter, these
8: //! checks use pattern-based heuristics — detecting System object patterns
9: //! based on common conventions (classes ending in "System", method calls
10: //! like `step()`, `setup()`, `release()`, property access patterns).
11: //!
12: //! ## Checks
13: //!
14: //! | ID | Severity | Description |
15: //! |----|----------|-------------|
16: //! | SONUMIN | Error | Wrong number of inputs to System object method |
17: //! | SONUMOUT | Error | Wrong number of outputs from System object method |
18: //! | SODEPPROP | Warning | Deprecated system object property |
19: //! | SOINITPROP | Warning | Property should be set in constructor |
20: //! | SODFLTVAL | Warning | Default value issue in system object |
21: //! | SORSRVDNM | Warning | Reserved name used for system object member |
22: //! | SOTUNPROP1 | Warning | Tunable property issue |
23: //! | SOTUNPROP3 | Warning | Non-tunable property modified after setup |
24: //! | SOTUNPROP4 | Error | Non-tunable property modified in step method |
25: //!
26: //! ## Configuration
27: //!
28: //! ```toml
29: //! [lint.rules.SYSTEM_OBJECTS_ENGINE]
30: //! skip_checks = ["SONUMIN"]
31: //! ```
32: //!
33: //! ## Limitations
34: //!
35: //! Without runtime type information, these checks rely on heuristics:
36: //! - Method names (`step`, `setup`, `release`, `reset`) suggest System object usage
37: //! - Class names containing "System" or inheriting from `matlab.System`
38: //! - Property access patterns on objects that appear to be System objects
39: //!
40: //! False positives are possible for non-System classes using similar method names.

126: /// Engine covering 9 system object validation checks.
127: ///
128: /// Uses pattern-based heuristics since full type information is not available.
129: /// Node-level checks fire on `function_call` nodes. File-level checks
130: /// analyze class definitions for property and method patterns.
131: pub struct SystemObjectsEngine {
132:     config: SystemObjectsEngineConfig,
133: }
134: 
135: /// Node types for node-level dispatch.
136: const TARGET_NODES: &[&str] = &["function_call"];

138: impl SystemObjectsEngine {
139:     /// Factory constructor called by the rule registry.
140:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
141:         let rule_config: SystemObjectsEngineConfig = config.rule_params("SYSTEM_OBJECTS_ENGINE");
142:         Box::new(Self {
143:             config: rule_config,
144:         })
145:     }
146: 
147:     /// Whether a check ID is enabled (not in `skip_checks`).
148:     fn is_enabled(&self, check_id: &str) -> bool {
149:         !self.config.skip_checks.iter().any(|s| s == check_id)
150:     }
151: 
152:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
153:     // Node-level check dispatchers
154:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
155: 
156:     /// Check a `function_call` node for system object method patterns.
157:     fn check_function_call<'a>(
158:         &self,
159:         node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>,
160:         source: &'a str,
161:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
162:         let mut diags = Vec::new();
163: 
164:         let func_name = match extract_func_name(node, source) {
165:             Some(n) => n,
166:             None => return diags,
167:         };
168: 
169:         // Detect method calls on objects: obj.step(), obj.setup(), etc.
170:         // In tree-sitter-matlab, these may appear as field_expression function_calls
171:         // where the name is like "obj.step"
172:         if let Some(method_name) = func_name.rsplit('.').next() {
173:             if SYSTEM_OBJECT_METHODS.contains(&method_name) {
174:                 // SONUMIN: Check argument count for step() method
175:                 // step() should have the System object + input signals
176:                 if self.is_enabled("SONUMIN") && method_name == "step" {
177:                     let arg_count = count_args(node);
178:                     // step() with no arguments is suspicious (should have at least input)
179:                     if arg_count == 0 && !func_name.contains('.') {
180:                         diags.push(make_diag("SONUMIN", node));
181:                     }
182:                 }
183: 
184:                 // SONUMOUT: Calling release()/reset() with output arguments
185:                 if self.is_enabled("SONUMOUT")
186:                     && (method_name == "release" || method_name == "reset")
187:                     && has_output_assignment(node) {
188:                         diags.push(make_diag("SONUMOUT", node));
189:                     }
190:             }
191:         }
192: 
193:         // SODEPPROP: Detect access to deprecated properties
194:         // Pattern: obj.SampleRate, obj.FrameLength, etc.
195:         if self.is_enabled("SODEPPROP") && func_name.contains('.') {
196:             if let Some(prop_name) = func_name.rsplit('.').next() {
197:                 if DEPRECATED_PROPERTIES.iter().any(|(p, _)| *p == prop_name) {
198:                     diags.push(make_diag("SODEPPROP", node));
199:                 }
200:             }
201:         }
202: 
203:         diags
204:     }
205:

207:     // File-level checks
208:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------

210:     /// File-level checks for class definitions inheriting from matlab.System.
211:     fn check_file_level(
212:         &self,
213:         tree: &tree_sitter::Tree,
214:         source: &str,
215:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
216:         let mut diags = Vec::new();
217:         let root = tree.root_node();
218: 
219:         // Find class definitions that inherit from matlab.System
220:         self.find_system_classes(&root, source, &mut diags);
221: 
222:         diags
223:     }

225:     /// Find class definitions and check for system object patterns.
226:     fn find_system_classes(
227:         &self,
228:         node: &tree_sitter::Node,
229:         source: &str,
230:         diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
231:     ) {
232:         let count = node.child_count();
233:         for i in 0..count {
234:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
235:                 if child.kind() == "class_definition" {
236:                     // Check if this class inherits from matlab.System
237:                     if is_system_object_class(child, source) {
238:                         self.check_system_class(child, source, diags);
239:                     }
240:                 }
241:                 self.find_system_classes(&child, source, diags);
242:             }
243:         }
244:     }
245: 
246:     /// Check a System object class for various issues.
247:     fn check_system_class(
248:         &self,
249:         class_node: tree_sitter::Node,
250:         source: &str,
251:         diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
252:     ) {
253:         let count = class_node.child_count();
254:         for i in 0..count {
255:             if let Some(child) = class_node.child(i) {
256:                 // SORSRVDNM: Check method names against reserved names
257:                 if self.is_enabled("SORSRVDNM") && child.kind() == "methods" {
258:                     self.check_reserved_method_names(child, source, diags);
259:                 }
260: 
261:                 // SODFLTVAL: Check properties for default value issues
262:                 if self.is_enabled("SODFLTVAL") && child.kind() == "properties" {
263:                     self.check_property_defaults(child, source, diags);
264:                 }
265:             }
266:         }
267:     }
268: 
269:     /// Check method names against reserved System object names.
270:     fn check_reserved_method_names(
271:         &self,
272:         methods_node: tree_sitter::Node,
273:         source: &str,
274:         diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
275:     ) {
276:         let count = methods_node.child_count();
277:         for i in 0..count {
278:             if let Some(child) = methods_node.child(i) {
279:                 if child.kind() == "function_definition" {
280:                     if let Some(name_node) = child.child_by_field_name("name") {
281:                         let method_name = node_text(name_node, source);
282:                         // Only flag if the method name is reserved but not an expected
283:                         // override (setupImpl, stepImpl, etc. are expected)
284:                         if RESERVED_NAMES.contains(&method_name)
285:                             && !method_name.ends_with("Impl")
286:                         {
287:                             diags.push(make_diag("SORSRVDNM", name_node));
288:                         }
289:                     }
290:                 }
291:             }
292:         }
293:     }
294: 
295:     /// Check property definitions for default value issues.
296:     fn check_property_defaults(
297:         &self,
298:         properties_node: tree_sitter::Node,
299:         source: &str,
300:         diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
301:     ) {
302:         let count = properties_node.child_count();
303:         for i in 0..count {
304:             if let Some(child) = properties_node.child(i) {
305:                 if child.kind() == "property" {
306:                     // Check for function call as default value (potentially problematic)
307:                     let text = node_text(child, source);
308:                     if text.contains('(') && text.contains(')') && text.contains('=') {
309:                         // Heuristic: property with function call default value
310:                         // e.g., `Prop = someFunction()`
311:                         diags.push(make_diag("SODFLTVAL", child));
312:                     }
313:                 }
314:             }
315:         }
316:     }
317: }

360: /// Build a diagnostic from a check ID and node, using the check's own severity.
361: fn make_diag(check_id: &'static str, node: tree_sitter::Node) -> Diagnostic {
362:     let start = node.start_position();
363:     Diagnostic {
364:         rule_id: check_id,
365:         message: check_description(check_id).to_string(),
366:         severity: check_severity(check_id),
367:         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
368:         line: start.row + 1,
369:         column: start.column + 1,
370:         fix: None,
371:     }
372: }

375: // Helper: node text extraction
376: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

378: /// Extract the raw text of a node.
379: fn node_text<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
380:     &source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()]
381: }
382: 
383: /// Extract function name from a `function_call` node.
384: fn extract_func_name<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
385:     if node.kind() != "function_call" {
386:         return None;
387:     }
388:     let name_node = node.child_by_field_name("name")?;
389:     Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
390: }

392: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
393: // Helper: pattern detection
394: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
395: 
396: /// Count the number of arguments in a `function_call` node.
397: fn count_args(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> usize {
398:     // In tree-sitter-matlab call arguments are a child node of kind
399:     // `arguments` rather than a named field, so `child_by_field_name` never
400:     // matches. Locate them by child kind instead.
401:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
402:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
403:         if child.kind() == "arguments" {
404:             return child.named_child_count();
405:         }
406:     }
407:     0
408: }
409: 
410: /// Check if a function_call is the RHS of an assignment (has output).
411: fn has_output_assignment(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
412:     if let Some(parent) = node.parent() {
413:         // Check if parent is an assignment and this node is on the right side
414:         if parent.kind() == "assignment" {
415:             if let Some(rhs) = parent.child_by_field_name("right").or_else(|| parent.child(2)) {
416:                 return node.start_byte() >= rhs.start_byte()
417:                     && node.end_byte() <= rhs.end_byte();
418:             }
419:         }
420:     }
421:     false
422: }
423: 
424: /// Check if a class definition inherits from matlab.System.
425: fn is_system_object_class(class_node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
426:     // Look for superclasses node containing "matlab.System"
427:     let count = class_node.child_count();
428:     for i in 0..count {
429:         if let Some(child) = class_node.child(i) {
430:             if child.kind() == "superclasses" {
431:                 let text = node_text(child, source);
432:                 if text.contains("matlab.System") {
433:                     return true;
434:                 }
435:             }
436:         }
437:     }
438:     false
439: }

    node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>,

) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {

        Some(n) => n,
        None => return diags,
    };

    // In tree-sitter-matlab, these may appear as field_expression function_calls

    if let Some(method_name) = func_name.rsplit('.').next() {

                if arg_count == 0 && !func_name.contains('.') {
                    diags.push(make_diag("SONUMIN", node));

            }

            // SONUMOUT: Calling release()/reset() with output arguments
            if self.is_enabled("SONUMOUT")

                    diags.push(make_diag("SONUMOUT", node));

    if self.is_enabled("SODEPPROP") && func_name.contains('.') {

                diags.push(make_diag("SODEPPROP", node));
            }
        }
    }

    diags

//! # SYSTEM_OBJECTS_ENGINE: System Object Validation Checks
//!
//! Implements 9 checks for MATLAB System object validation. System objects
//! (classes inheriting from `matlab.System`) have specific lifecycle
//! constraints that static analysis can partially verify.
//!
//! Since full type information is not available to a static linter, these
//! checks use pattern-based heuristics — detecting System object patterns
//! based on common conventions (classes ending in "System", method calls
//! like `step()`, `setup()`, `release()`, property access patterns).
//!
//! ## Checks
//!
//! | ID | Severity | Description |
//! |----|----------|-------------|
//! | SONUMIN | Error | Wrong number of inputs to System object method |
//! | SONUMOUT | Error | Wrong number of outputs from System object method |
//! | SODEPPROP | Warning | Deprecated system object property |
//! | SOINITPROP | Warning | Property should be set in constructor |
//! | SODFLTVAL | Warning | Default value issue in system object |
//! | SORSRVDNM | Warning | Reserved name used for system object member |
//! | SOTUNPROP1 | Warning | Tunable property issue |
//! | SOTUNPROP3 | Warning | Non-tunable property modified after setup |
//! | SOTUNPROP4 | Error | Non-tunable property modified in step method |
//!
//! ## Configuration
//!
//! ```toml
//! [lint.rules.SYSTEM_OBJECTS_ENGINE]
//! skip_checks = ["SONUMIN"]
//! ```
//!
//! ## Limitations
//!
//! Without runtime type information, these checks rely on heuristics:
//! - Method names (`step`, `setup`, `release`, `reset`) suggest System object usage
//! - Class names containing "System" or inheriting from `matlab.System`
//! - Property access patterns on objects that appear to be System objects
//!
//! False positives are possible for non-System classes using similar method names.
//!
//! The engine is split across one module per independent check:
//! - [`check_sonumin`] — SONUMIN
//! - [`check_sonumout`] — SONUMOUT
//! - [`check_sodeprop`] — SODEPPROP
//! - [`check_sorsrvdnm`] — SORSRVDNM
//! - [`check_sodfltval`] — SODFLTVAL

    #[serde(default)]
    pub skip_checks: Vec<String>,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Static metadata for a single system object check.
pub(crate) struct CheckMeta {
    id: &'static str,
    severity: Severity,
    description: &'static str,
}

/// All 9 system object check definitions.
pub(crate) const CHECKS: &[CheckMeta] = &[
    CheckMeta { id: "SONUMIN", severity: Severity::Error, description: "System object method called with wrong number of inputs" },
    ...
];

/// System object lifecycle methods.
pub(crate) const SYSTEM_OBJECT_METHODS: &[&str] = &[

/// Engine covering 9 system object validation checks.
///
/// Uses pattern-based heuristics since full type information is not available.
/// Node-level checks fire on `function_call` nodes. File-level checks
/// analyze class definitions for property and method patterns.
pub struct SystemObjectsEngine {
    config: SystemObjectsEngineConfig,
}

/// Node types for node-level dispatch.
const TARGET_NODES: &[&str] = &["function_call"];

impl SystemObjectsEngine {
    /// Factory constructor called by the rule registry.
    pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
        let rule_config: SystemObjectsEngineConfig = config.rule_params("SYSTEM_OBJECTS_ENGINE");
        Box::new(Self {
            config: rule_config,
        })
    }

    /// Whether a check ID is enabled (not in `skip_checks`).
    pub(crate) fn is_enabled(&self, check_id: &str) -> bool {
        !self.config.skip_checks.iter().any(|s| s == check_id)
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Node-level check dispatchers
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------

    /// Check a `function_call` node for system object method patterns.
    fn check_function_call<'a>(
        &self,
        node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>,
        source: &'a str,
    ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
        let mut diags = Vec::new();

        let func_name = match extract_func_name(node, source) {
            Some(n) => n,
            None => return diags,
        };

        // Detect method calls on objects: obj.step(), obj.setup(), etc.
        // In tree-sitter-matlab, these may appear as field_expression function_calls
        // where the name is like "obj.step"
        if let Some(method_name) = func_name.rsplit('.').next() {
            if SYSTEM_OBJECT_METHODS.contains(&method_name) {
                diags.extend(self.check_sonumin(node, func_name, method_name));
                diags.extend(self.check_sonumout(node, method_name));
            }
        }

        diags.extend(self.check_sodeprop(node, func_name));

        diags
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // File-level checks
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------

    /// File-level checks for class definitions inheriting from matlab.System.
    fn check_file_level(
        &self,
        tree: &tree_sitter::Tree,
        source: &str,
    ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
        let mut diags = Vec::new();
        let root = tree.root_node();

        // Find class definitions that inherit from matlab.System
        self.find_system_classes(&root, source, &mut diags);

        diags
    }

    /// Find class definitions and check for system object patterns.
    fn find_system_classes(
        &self,
        node: &tree_sitter::Node,
        source: &str,
        diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
    ) {
        let count = node.child_count();
        for i in 0..count {
            if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
                if child.kind() == "class_definition" {
                    // Check if this class inherits from matlab.System
                    if is_system_object_class(child, source) {
                        self.check_system_class(child, source, diags);
                    }
                }
                self.find_system_classes(&child, source, diags);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Check a System object class for various issues.
    fn check_system_class(
        &self,
        class_node: tree_sitter::Node,
        source: &str,
        diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
    ) {
        let count = class_node.child_count();
        for i in 0..count {
            if let Some(child) = class_node.child(i) {
                // SORSRVDNM: Check method names against reserved names
                if self.is_enabled("SORSRVDNM") && child.kind() == "methods" {
                    self.check_sorsrvdnm(child, source, diags);
                }

                // SODFLTVAL: Check properties for default value issues
                if self.is_enabled("SODFLTVAL") && child.kind() == "properties" {
                    self.check_sodfltval(child, source, diags);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

    /// Check method names against reserved System object names.
    pub(crate) fn check_sorsrvdnm(
        &self,
        methods_node: tree_sitter::Node,
        source: &str,
        diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
    ) {
        let count = methods_node.child_count();
        for i in 0..count {
            if let Some(child) = methods_node.child(i) {
                if child.kind() == "function_definition" {
                    if let Some(name_node) = child.child_by_field_name("name") {
                        let method_name = node_text(name_node, source);
                        // Only flag if the method name is reserved but not an expected
                        // override (setupImpl, stepImpl, etc. are expected)
                        if RESERVED_NAMES.contains(&method_name)
                            && !method_name.ends_with("Impl")
                        {
                            diags.push(make_diag("SORSRVDNM", name_node));
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

//! # SYSTEM_OBJECTS_ENGINE: System Object Validation Checks
//!
//! Implements 9 checks for MATLAB System object validation. System objects
//! (classes inheriting from `matlab.System`) have specific lifecycle
//! constraints that static analysis can partially verify.
//!
//! Since full type information is not available to a static linter, these
//! checks use pattern-based heuristics — detecting System object patterns
//! based on common conventions (classes ending in "System", method calls
//! like `step()`, `setup()`, `release()`, property access patterns).
//!
//! ## Checks
//!
//! | ID | Severity | Description |
//! |----|----------|-------------|
//! | SONUMIN | Error | Wrong number of inputs to System object method |
//! | SONUMOUT | Error | Wrong number of outputs from System object method |
//! | SODEPPROP | Warning | Deprecated system object property |
//! | SOINITPROP | Warning | Property should be set in constructor |
//! | SODFLTVAL | Warning | Default value issue in system object |
//! | SORSRVDNM | Warning | Reserved name used for system object member |
//! | SOTUNPROP1 | Warning | Tunable property issue |
//! | SOTUNPROP3 | Warning | Non-tunable property modified after setup |
//! | SOTUNPROP4 | Error | Non-tunable property modified in step method |
//!
//! ## Configuration
//!
//! ```toml
//! [lint.rules.SYSTEM_OBJECTS_ENGINE]
//! skip_checks = ["SONUMIN"]
//! ```
//!
//! ## Limitations
//!
//! Without runtime type information, these checks rely on heuristics:
//! - Method names (`step`, `setup`, `release`, `reset`) suggest System object usage
//! - Class names containing "System" or inheriting from `matlab.System`
//! - Property access patterns on objects that appear to be System objects
//!
//! False positives are possible for non-System classes using similar method names.

mod check_sodeprop;
mod check_sodfltval;
mod check_sonumin;
mod check_sonumout;
mod check_sorsrvdnm;

use mlt_core::{Category, Config, Diagnostic, FileContext, NodeContext, Rule, Severity};
use serde::Deserialize;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Rule-specific configuration
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Configuration for the system objects engine.
///
/// Deserialized from the `[lint.rules.SYSTEM_OBJECTS_ENGINE]` section in `.mlt.toml`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Default)]
pub struct SystemObjectsEngineConfig {
    /// Check IDs to skip (e.g., `["SONUMIN"]`).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub skip_checks: Vec<String>,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Check metadata
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Static metadata for a single system object check.
pub(crate) struct CheckMeta {
    id: &'static str,
    severity: Severity,
    description: &'static str,
}

/// All 9 system object check definitions.
pub(crate) const CHECKS: &[CheckMeta] = &[
    CheckMeta { id: "SONUMIN", severity: Severity::Error, description: "System object method called with wrong number of inputs" },
    CheckMeta { id: "SONUMOUT", severity: Severity::Error, description: "System object method called with wrong number of outputs" },
    CheckMeta { id: "SODEPPROP", severity: Severity::Warning, description: "Deprecated system object property; use the recommended replacement" },
    CheckMeta { id: "SOINITPROP", severity: Severity::Warning, description: "System object property should be set in the constructor, not after construction" },
    CheckMeta { id: "SODFLTVAL", severity: Severity::Warning, description: "System object property default value may cause unexpected behavior" },
    CheckMeta { id: "SORSRVDNM", severity: Severity::Warning, description: "Reserved name used for system object member; choose a different name" },
    CheckMeta { id: "SOTUNPROP1", severity: Severity::Warning, description: "Tunable property constraint may be violated" },
    CheckMeta { id: "SOTUNPROP3", severity: Severity::Warning, description: "Non-tunable property should not be modified after setup() is called" },
    CheckMeta { id: "SOTUNPROP4", severity: Severity::Error, description: "Non-tunable property must not be modified inside the step() method" },
];

/// System object lifecycle methods.
pub(crate) const SYSTEM_OBJECT_METHODS: &[&str] = &[
    "step", "setup", "release", "reset", "isDone", "isLocked",
    "getNumInputs", "getNumOutputs", "clone",
];

/// Reserved System object method names that should not be overridden.
pub(crate) const RESERVED_NAMES: &[&str] = &[
    "step", "setup", "release", "reset", "isDone", "isLocked",
    "getNumInputs", "getNumOutputs", "clone",
    "processTunedPropertiesImpl", "infoImpl",
];

/// Deprecated System object properties and their replacements.
pub(crate) const DEPRECATED_PROPERTIES: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
    ("SampleRate", "use getSampleRate method"),
    ("FrameLength", "set via input signal"),
    ("NumChannels", "determined automatically from input"),
];

/// Look up check metadata by ID.
pub(crate) fn check_meta(id: &str) -> Option<&'static CheckMeta> {
    CHECKS.iter().find(|c| c.id == id)
}

/// Look up check description by ID.
pub(crate) fn check_description(id: &str) -> &'static str {
    check_meta(id)
        .map(|c| c.description)
        .unwrap_or("System object validation issue")
}

/// Look up check severity by ID.
pub(crate) fn check_severity(id: &str) -> Severity {
    check_meta(id)
        .map(|c| c.severity)
        .unwrap_or(Severity::Warning)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Rule implementation
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Engine covering 9 system object validation checks.
///
/// Uses pattern-based heuristics since full type information is not available.
/// Node-level checks fire on `function_call` nodes. File-level checks
/// analyze class definitions for property and method patterns.
pub struct SystemObjectsEngine {
    config: SystemObjectsEngineConfig,
}

/// Node types for node-level dispatch.
const TARGET_NODES: &[&str] = &["function_call"];

impl SystemObjectsEngine {
    /// Factory constructor called by the rule registry.
    pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
        let rule_config: SystemObjectsEngineConfig = config.rule_params("SYSTEM_OBJECTS_ENGINE");
        Box::new(Self {
            config: rule_config,
        })
    }

    /// Whether a check ID is enabled (not in `skip_checks`).
    pub(crate) fn is_enabled(&self, check_id: &str) -> bool {
        !self.config.skip_checks.iter().any(|s| s == check_id)
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Node-level check dispatchers
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------

    /// Check a `function_call` node for system object method patterns.
    fn check_function_call<'a>(
        &self,
        node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>,
        source: &'a str,
    ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
        let mut diags = Vec::new();

        let func_name = match extract_func_name(node, source) {
            Some(n) => n,
            None => return diags,
        };

        // Detect method calls on objects: obj.step(), obj.setup(), etc.
        // In tree-sitter-matlab, these may appear as field_expression function_calls
        // where the name is like "obj.step"
        if let Some(method_name) = func_name.rsplit('.').next() {
            if SYSTEM_OBJECT_METHODS.contains(&method_name) {
                diags.extend(self.check_sonumin(node, func_name, method_name));
                diags.extend(self.check_sonumout(node, method_name));
            }
        }

        diags.extend(self.check_sodeprop(node, func_name));

        diags
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // File-level checks
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------

    /// File-level checks for class definitions inheriting from matlab.System.
    fn check_file_level(
        &self,
        tree: &tree_sitter::Tree,
        source: &str,
    ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
        let mut diags = Vec::new();
        let root = tree.root_node();

        // Find class definitions that inherit from matlab.System
        self.find_system_classes(&root, source, &mut diags);

        diags
    }

    /// Find class definitions and check for system object patterns.
    fn find_system_classes(
        &self,
        node: &tree_sitter::Node,
        source: &str,
        diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
    ) {
        let count = node.child_count();
        for i in 0..count {
            if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
                if child.kind() == "class_definition" {
                    // Check if this class inherits from matlab.System
                    if is_system_object_class(child, source) {
                        self.check_system_class(child, source, diags);
                    }
                }
                self.find_system_classes(&child, source, diags);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Check a System object class for various issues.
    fn check_system_class(
        &self,
        class_node: tree_sitter::Node,
        source: &str,
        diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
    ) {
        let count = class_node.child_count();
        for i in 0..count {
            if let Some(child) = class_node.child(i) {
                // SORSRVDNM: Check method names against reserved names
                if self.is_enabled("SORSRVDNM") && child.kind() == "methods" {
                    self.check_sorsrvdnm(child, source, diags);
                }

                // SODFLTVAL: Check properties for default value issues
                if self.is_enabled("SODFLTVAL") && child.kind() == "properties" {
                    self.check_sodfltval(child, source, diags);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

impl Rule for SystemObjectsEngine {
    fn id(&self) -> &'static str {
        "SYSTEM_OBJECTS_ENGINE"
    }

    fn description(&self) -> &'static str {
        "System object validation checks"
    }

    fn severity(&self) -> Severity {
        Severity::Warning
    }

    fn category(&self) -> Category {
        Category::SystemObjects
    }

    fn target_node_types(&self) -> &'static [&'static str] {
        TARGET_NODES
    }

    fn has_file_check(&self) -> bool {
        true
    }

    fn check(&self, ctx: &NodeContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
        match ctx.node.kind() {
            "function_call" => self.check_function_call(ctx.node, ctx.source),
            _ => Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    fn check_file(&self, ctx: &FileContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
        self.check_file_level(ctx.tree, ctx.source)
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helper: diagnostic construction
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Build a diagnostic from a check ID and node, using the check's own severity.
pub(crate) fn make_diag(check_id: &'static str, node: tree_sitter::Node) -> Diagnostic {
    let start = node.start_position();
    Diagnostic {
        rule_id: check_id,
        message: check_description(check_id).to_string(),
        severity: check_severity(check_id),
        byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
        line: start.row + 1,
        column: start.column + 1,
        fix: None,
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helper: node text extraction
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Extract the raw text of a node.
pub(crate) fn node_text<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
    &source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()]
}

/// Extract function name from a `function_call` node.
pub(crate) fn extract_func_name<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
    if node.kind() != "function_call" {
        return None;
    }
    let name_node = node.child_by_field_name("name")?;
    Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helper: pattern detection
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Count the number of arguments in a `function_call` node.
pub(crate) fn count_args(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> usize {
    // In tree-sitter-matlab call arguments are a child node of kind
    // `arguments` rather than a named field, so `child_by_field_name` never
    // matches. Locate them by child kind instead.
    let mut cursor = node.walk();
    for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
        if child.kind() == "arguments" {
            return child.named_child_count();
        }
    }
    0
}

/// Check if a function_call is the RHS of an assignment (has output).
pub(crate) fn has_output_assignment(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
    if let Some(parent) = node.parent() {
        // Check if parent is an assignment and this node is on the right side
        if parent.kind() == "assignment" {
            if let Some(rhs) = parent.child_by_field_name("right").or_else(|| parent.child(2)) {
                return node.start_byte() >= rhs.start_byte()
                    && node.end_byte() <= rhs.end_byte();
            }
        }
    }
    false
}

/// Check if a class definition inherits from matlab.System.
pub(crate) fn is_system_object_class(class_node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
    // Look for superclasses node containing "matlab.System"
    let count = class_node.child_count();
    for i in 0..count {
        if let Some(child) = class_node.child(i) {
            if child.kind() == "superclasses" {
                let text = node_text(child, source);
                if text.contains("matlab.System") {
                    return true;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    false
}

import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ORIG = ROOT / "system_objects.rs"
DIR = ROOT / "system_objects"

failures = []


def fail(msg):
    failures.append(msg)
    print(f"  FAIL: {msg}")


def ok(msg):
    print(f"  ok: {msg}")


def normalize(text: str) -> str:
    """Strip leading whitespace per line, drop blank lines and comment-only lines."""
    lines = []
    for ln in text.splitlines():
        s = ln.strip()
        if not s:
            continue
        lines.append(s)
    return "\n".join(lines)


def find_brace_block(text: str, open_idx: int) -> str:
    """Return text from the `{` at open_idx through its matching `}` (inclusive)."""
    depth = 0
    i = open_idx
    n = len(text)
    while i < n:
        c = text[i]
        if c == "{":
            depth += 1
        elif c == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return text[open_idx:i + 1]
        i += 1
    raise RuntimeError("unbalanced braces")


def extract_fn_body(text: str, fn_name: str) -> str:
    """Extract the body (braces only, from `{` after signature to matching `}`) of fn."""
    m = re.search(r"\bfn\s+" + re.escape(fn_name) + r"\b", text)
    if not m:
        raise RuntimeError(f"fn {fn_name} not found")
    open_idx = text.index("{", m.end())
    return find_brace_block(text, open_idx)


def extract_if_block_from(text: str, anchor: str) -> str:
    """Extract a complete `if` statement starting at the first `if` after `anchor`,
    including preceding comment lines that directly lead into it."""
    start = text.index(anchor)
    if_start = text.index("if", start)
    # include contiguous comment lines immediately before the `if`
    line_start = text.rfind("\n", 0, if_start) + 1
    # walk back over comment lines
    prefix_lines = []
    pos = line_start
    while True:
        prev_nl = text.rfind("\n", 0, pos - 1)
        if prev_nl == -1:
            break
        prev_line = text[prev_nl + 1:pos - 1]
        if prev_line.strip().startswith("//"):
            prefix_lines.insert(0, prev_nl + 1)
            pos = prev_nl + 1
        else:
            break
    block_start = prefix_lines[0] if prefix_lines else line_start
    open_idx = text.index("{", if_start)
    return text[block_start:text.index("}", text.index("}", open_idx)) + 1]

orig = ORIG.read_text()

#     and check_property_defaults -> check_sodfltval

    new_body = extract_fn_body(new_file.read_text(), new_name)
    if normalize(orig_body) == normalize(new_body):
        ok(f"{orig_name} -> {new_name}: bodies identical (mod indentation)")
    else:
        fail(f"{orig_name} -> {new_name}: bodies DIFFER")
        print("--- original ---")
        print(normalize(orig_body))
        print("--- new ---")
        print(normalize(new_body))

    ("SONUMOUT block -> check_sonumout", "// SONUMOUT: Calling release()/reset()", DIR / "check_sonumout.rs"),
    ("SODEPPROP block -> check_sodeprop", "// SODEPPROP: Detect access to deprecated", DIR / "check_sodeprop.rs"),

check_ids = ["SONUMIN", "SONUMOUT", "SODEPPROP", "SORSRVDNM", "SODFLTVAL"]

else:

orig_tests = len(re.findall(r"#\[test\]", orig))
moved_tests = sum(len(re.findall(r"#\[test\]", p.read_text())) for p in DIR.glob("check_*.rs"))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verification for the system_objects.rs → system_objects/ mechanical split.

Checks:
1. Moved method bodies match the original (modulo `pub(crate)` and indentation).
2. Each check ID's `make_diag("ID", ...)` appears exactly once across system_objects/.
3. Dispatch references in mod.rs match the moved methods (and no stale references
   in the NEW files).
4. Moved-test count equals the original test count.
5. Original system_objects.rs is untouched (matches HEAD, no diff).
"""
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/home/watermarkhu/repositories/mlt/crates/mlt_rules/src")
ORIG = ROOT / "system_objects.rs"
DIR = ROOT / "system_objects"

failures = []


def fail(msg):
    failures.append(msg)
    print(f"  FAIL: {msg}")


def ok(msg):
    print(f"  ok: {msg}")


def normalize(text: str) -> str:
    """Strip leading whitespace per line, drop blank lines."""
    lines = []
    for ln in text.splitlines():
        s = ln.strip()
        if not s:
            continue
        lines.append(s)
    return "\n".join(lines)


def find_brace_block(text: str, open_idx: int) -> str:
    """Return text from the `{` at open_idx through its matching `}` (inclusive)."""
    depth = 0
    i = open_idx
    n = len(text)
    while i < n:
        c = text[i]
        if c == "{":
            depth += 1
        elif c == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return text[open_idx:i + 1]
        i += 1
    raise RuntimeError("unbalanced braces")


def extract_fn_body(text: str, fn_name: str) -> str:
    """Extract the body (from `{` after signature to matching `}`) of fn `fn_name`."""
    m = re.search(r"\bfn\s+" + re.escape(fn_name) + r"\b", text)
    if not m:
        raise RuntimeError(f"fn {fn_name} not found")
    open_idx = text.index("{", m.end())
    return find_brace_block(text, open_idx)


def extract_if_with_comments(text: str, anchor: str) -> str:
    """Extract a complete `if` statement plus any contiguous comment lines
    immediately preceding it, starting the search at `anchor`."""
    start = text.index(anchor)
    if_start = text.index("if", start)
    open_idx = text.index("{", if_start)
    block = find_brace_block(text, open_idx)
    block_end = open_idx + len(block)
    # walk back over contiguous comment lines immediately before the `if`
    pos = if_start
    while True:
        prev_nl = text.rfind("\n", 0, pos - 1)
        if prev_nl == -1:
            break
        prev_line = text[prev_nl + 1:pos - 1]
        if prev_line.strip().startswith("//"):
            pos = prev_nl + 1
        else:
            break
    return text[pos:block_end]


print("== 1. Moved method bodies match original ==")
orig = ORIG.read_text()

# 1a. Full-method moves: check_reserved_method_names -> check_sorsrvdnm
#     and check_property_defaults -> check_sodfltval
for orig_name, new_name, new_file in [
    ("check_reserved_method_names", "check_sorsrvdnm", DIR / "check_sorsrvdnm.rs"),
    ("check_property_defaults", "check_sodfltval", DIR / "check_sodfltval.rs"),
]:
    orig_body = extract_fn_body(orig, orig_name)
    new_body = extract_fn_body(new_file.read_text(), new_name)
    if normalize(orig_body) == normalize(new_body):
        ok(f"{orig_name} -> {new_name}: bodies identical (mod indentation)")
    else:
        fail(f"{orig_name} -> {new_name}: bodies DIFFER")

# 1b. Extracted blocks from check_function_call -> check_sonumin/check_sonumout/check_sodeprop
extractions = [
    ("SONUMIN block -> check_sonumin", "// SONUMIN: Check argument count", DIR / "check_sonumin.rs", "SONUMIN"),
    ("SONUMOUT block -> check_sonumout", "// SONUMOUT: Calling release()/reset()", DIR / "check_sonumout.rs", "SONUMOUT"),
    ("SODEPPROP block -> check_sodeprop", "// SODEPPROP: Detect access to deprecated", DIR / "check_sodeprop.rs", "SODEPPROP"),
]
fc_text = orig[orig.index("fn check_function_call"):]
for label, anchor, new_file, _cid in extractions:
    orig_block = extract_if_with_comments(fc_text, anchor)
    new_text = new_file.read_text()
    new_block = extract_if_with_comments(new_text, anchor)
    if normalize(orig_block) == normalize(new_block):
        ok(f"{label}: identical (mod indentation)")
    else:
        fail(f"{label}: DIFFER")
        print("--- original ---")
        print(normalize(orig_block))
        print("--- new ---")
        print(normalize(new_block))

print()
print("== 2. Each check ID's make_diag appears exactly once ==")
check_ids = ["SONUMIN", "SONUMOUT", "SODEPPROP", "SORSRVDNM", "SODFLTVAL"]
all_text = "\n".join(p.read_text() for p in DIR.glob("*.rs"))
for cid in check_ids:
    count = len(re.findall(rf'make_diag\("{cid}"', all_text))
    if count == 1:
        ok(f"{cid}: exactly one make_diag call")
    else:
        fail(f"{cid}: make_diag count = {count}")

# every check ID in the CHECKS metadata is still listed in mod.rs CHECKS
mod_rs = (DIR / "mod.rs").read_text()
all_nine = ["SONUMIN", "SONUMOUT", "SODEPPROP", "SOINITPROP", "SODFLTVAL",
            "SORSRVDNM", "SOTUNPROP1", "SOTUNPROP3", "SOTUNPROP4"]
for cid in all_nine:
    if len(re.findall(rf'\b{cid}\b', mod_rs)) >= 1:
        ok(f"{cid} present in mod.rs metadata")
    else:
        fail(f"{cid} missing from mod.rs")

print()
print("== 3. Dispatch references match ==")
for cid, meth in [
    ("SONUMIN", "check_sonumin"),
    ("SONUMOUT", "check_sonumout"),
    ("SODEPPROP", "check_sodeprop"),
    ("SORSRVDNM", "check_sorsrvdnm"),
    ("SODFLTVAL", "check_sodfltval"),
]:
    defs = []
    for p in DIR.glob("check_*.rs"):
        t = p.read_text()
        if re.search(rf"\bfn\s+{meth}\b", t):
            defs.append(p.name)
    if len(defs) == 1:
        ok(f"{meth} defined in {defs[0]}")
    else:
        fail(f"{meth} defined in {len(defs)} files: {defs}")
    refs = len(re.findall(rf"self\.{meth}\(", mod_rs))
    if refs >= 1:
        ok(f"mod.rs dispatches to {meth} ({refs} call site(s))")
    else:
        fail(f"mod.rs does NOT reference {meth}")

# no stale references to old method names in the NEW files (original is untouched by design)
stale = []
for p in DIR.glob("*.rs"):
    t = p.read_text()
    for old in ["check_reserved_method_names", "check_property_defaults"]:
        if re.search(rf"\b{old}\b", t):
            stale.append(f"{p.name}: {old}")
if stale:
    fail(f"stale references in new files: {stale}")
else:
    ok("no stale references to old method names in new system_objects/ files")

# new submodule declarations in mod.rs all exist as files
for p in DIR.glob("check_*.rs"):
    name = p.stem
    if re.search(rf"^\s*mod\s+{re.escape(name)};", mod_rs, re.MULTILINE):
        ok(f"mod.rs declares mod {name}")
    else:
        fail(f"mod.rs missing mod {name}")

print()
print("== 4. Test counts ==")
orig_tests = len(re.findall(r"#\[test\]", orig))
moved_tests = sum(len(re.findall(r"#\[test\]", p.read_text())) for p in DIR.glob("check_*.rs"))
mod_tests = len(re.findall(r"#\[test\]", mod_rs))
if orig_tests == moved_tests == 13 and mod_tests == 0:
    ok(f"original {orig_tests} tests == moved {moved_tests} tests; 0 left in mod.rs")
else:
    fail(f"original={orig_tests} moved={moved_tests} mod.rs={mod_tests}")

orig_test_names = re.findall(r"#\[test\]\n\s*fn\s+(\w+)", orig)
new_test_names = re.findall(r"#\[test\]\n\s*fn\s+(\w+)", all_text)
if sorted(orig_test_names) == sorted(new_test_names):
    ok(f"test names preserved: {len(orig_test_names)}")
else:
    missing = set(orig_test_names) - set(new_test_names)
    extra = set(new_test_names) - set(orig_test_names)
    fail(f"test name mismatch; missing={missing} extra={extra}")

print()
print("== 5. Original file untouched ==")
r = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "-C", "/home/watermarkhu/repositories/mlt", "diff", "--stat", "--",
     "crates/mlt_rules/src/system_objects.rs"],
    capture_output=True, text=True,
)
if r.stdout.strip():
    fail(f"system_objects.rs has uncommitted diff:\n{r.stdout}")
else:
    ok("system_objects.rs has no diff (untouched)")

print()
if failures:
    print(f"VERIFICATION FAILED: {len(failures)} issue(s)")
    sys.exit(1)
print("VERIFICATION PASSED")

5: //! while AGROW, SAGROW, and PFBNS require file-level traversal to detect
6: //! array growth patterns inside loops.
7: //!
8: //! ## Architecture
9: //!
10: //! A single `PerformanceEngine` struct handles all 41 checks. Node-level checks
11: //! are dispatched by node kind (`function_call`, `command`, `binary_operator`,
12: //! `boolean_operator`, `comparison_operator`). File-level checks traverse the
13: //! full tree looking for growth patterns inside `for_statement`/`while_statement`.
14: //!
15: //! ## Examples
16: //!
17: //! Bad:
18: //! ```matlab
19: //! for i = 1:n
20: //!     x = [x, val];          % AGROW
21: //! end
22: //! if a & b                   % AND2
23: //! inv(A) * b                 % MINV
24: //! exist('foo', 'file')       % EXIST
25: //! ```
26: //!
27: //! Good:
28: //! ```matlab
29: //! x = zeros(1, n);
30: //! for i = 1:n

121:     CheckMeta { id: "TRIM2",       description: "Use 'strip' instead of 'strtrim' for more flexible whitespace removal" },
122:     CheckMeta { id: "STTOK",       description: "Use 'split' instead of 'strtok' in a loop for better performance" },
123:     CheckMeta { id: "STNCI",       description: "Use 'strcmpi' instead of wrapping 'strcmp' with 'lower'" },
124:     CheckMeta { id: "STCCS",       description: "Use 'contains' instead of '~isempty(strfind(...))'" },
125:     CheckMeta { id: "FNDSB",       description: "Use 'contains' or 'matches' instead of 'findstr'" },
126: ];
127: 
128: /// Look up check description by ID.
129: pub(crate) fn check_description(id: &str) -> &'static str {
130:     CHECKS
131:         .iter()
132:         .find(|c| c.id == id)
133:         .map(|c| c.description)
134:         .unwrap_or("Performance improvement suggestion")
135: }

139: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

141: /// Hybrid performance engine covering 41 performance checks.
142: ///
143: /// Node-level checks fire on `function_call`, `command`, `binary_operator`,
144: /// `boolean_operator`, and `comparison_operator`. File-level checks (AGROW,
145: /// SAGROW, PFBNS) traverse the full tree for loop growth patterns.
146: pub struct PerformanceEngine {
147:     config: PerformanceEngineConfig,
148: }
149: 
150: /// Node types for node-level dispatch.
151: const TARGET_NODES: &[&str] = &[
152:     "function_call",
153:     "command",
154:     "binary_operator",
155:     "boolean_operator",
156:     "comparison_operator",
157:     "unary_operator",
158: ];
159: 
160: impl PerformanceEngine {
161:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
162:         let rule_config: PerformanceEngineConfig = config.rule_params("PERFORMANCE_ENGINE");
163:         Box::new(Self {
164:             config: rule_config,
165:         })
166:     }
167:     fn is_enabled(&self, check_id: &str) -> bool {
168:         !self.config.skip_checks.iter().any(|s| s == check_id)
169:     }
170: 
171:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
172:     // File-level checks: AGROW, SAGROW, PFBNS
173:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
174: 
175:     fn check_growth_in_loops(
176:         &self,
177:         tree: &tree_sitter::Tree,
178:         source: &str,
179:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
180:         let mut diags = Vec::new();
181:         let root = tree.root_node();
182:         self.traverse_for_growth(&root, source, false, &mut diags);
183:         diags
184:     }
185:     fn traverse_for_growth(
186:         &self,
187:         node: &tree_sitter::Node,
188:         source: &str,
189:         in_loop: bool,
190:         diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
191:     ) {
192:         let kind = node.kind();
193:         let entering_loop = kind == "for_statement" || kind == "while_statement";
194:         let now_in_loop = in_loop || entering_loop;
195: 
196:         // Only check assignment nodes inside loops.
197:         if now_in_loop && kind == "assignment" {
198:             self.check_assignment_growth(*node, source, diags);
199:         }
200: 
201:         // Also detect growth via full-node text for assignments that tree-sitter
202:         // may parse differently (e.g., s.field(end+1) = k might parse as
203:         // a function_call at statement level rather than an assignment).
204:         if now_in_loop
205:             && (kind == "function_call" || kind == "cell_index")
206:             && is_statement_level(node)
207:         {
208:             let text = node_text(*node, source);
209:             let normalized: String = text.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
210:             if normalized.contains("end+1") {
211:                 let has_dot = text.contains('.');
212:                 let check_id = if has_dot { "SAGROW" } else { "AGROW" };
213:                 if self.is_enabled(check_id) {
214:                     diags.push(make_diag(check_id, *node));
215:                 }
216:             }
217:         }
218: 
219:         let count = node.child_count();
220:         for i in 0..count {
221:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
222:                 self.traverse_for_growth(&child, source, now_in_loop, diags);
223:             }
224:         }
225:     }
226:     fn check_assignment_growth(
227:         &self,
228:         node: tree_sitter::Node,
229:         source: &str,
230:         diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
231:     ) {
232:         let lhs = match node.child_by_field_name("left").or_else(|| node.child(0)) {
233:             Some(n) => n,
234:             None => return,
235:         };
236:         let rhs = match node.child_by_field_name("right").or_else(|| node.child(2)) {
237:             Some(n) => n,
238:             None => return,
239:         };
240: 
241:         let lhs_text = node_text(lhs, source);
242:         let rhs_text = node_text(rhs, source);
243: 
244:         // Determine if LHS involves a struct field (for SAGROW vs AGROW).
245:         let is_struct = lhs.kind() == "field_expression"
246:             || (lhs.kind() == "function_call" && lhs_text.contains('.'));
247: 
248:         let check_id = if is_struct { "SAGROW" } else { "AGROW" };
249: 
250:         if !self.is_enabled(check_id) {
251:             return;
252:         }
253: 
254:         // Pattern 1: x(end+1) = ... or x{end+1} = ...
255:         // LHS is a function_call (indexing) or cell_index containing "end+1"
256:         // or "end + 1".
257:         if (lhs.kind() == "function_call" || lhs.kind() == "cell_index")
258:             && contains_end_plus_pattern(lhs, source)
259:         {
260:             diags.push(make_diag(check_id, node));
261:             return;
262:         }
263: 
264:         // Pattern 1b: s.field(end+1) = ... — may parse with field_expression as LHS
265:         // and end+1 in the assignment text before the `=`.
266:         if lhs.kind() == "field_expression" {
267:             // Check the full assignment text up to the `=` for end+1 pattern.
268:             let assign_text = node_text(node, source);
269:             if let Some(eq_pos) = assign_text.find('=') {
270:                 let lhs_full = &assign_text[..eq_pos];
271:                 let normalized: String = lhs_full.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
272:                 if normalized.contains("end+1") {
273:                     diags.push(make_diag("SAGROW", node));
274:                     return;
275:                 }
276:             }
277:         }
278: 
279:         // Pattern 2: x = [x, val] or x = [x; val]
280:         // LHS is a simple identifier, RHS is a matrix containing that identifier.
281:         if lhs.kind() == "identifier" {
282:             let var_name = lhs_text;
283:             if rhs.kind() == "matrix" && matrix_contains_var(rhs, source, var_name) {
284:                 diags.push(make_diag(check_id, node));
285:                 return;
286:             }
287:             // Also check cell: x = {x, val} — though less common
288:             if rhs.kind() == "cell" && matrix_contains_var(rhs, source, var_name) {
289:                 diags.push(make_diag(check_id, node));
290:                 return;
291:             }
292:         }
293: 
294:         // Pattern 3: s.field = [s.field, val]
295:         if lhs.kind() == "field_expression" {
296:             let field_text = lhs_text;
297:             if rhs.kind() == "matrix" && rhs_text.contains(field_text) {
298:                 diags.push(make_diag("SAGROW", node));
299:             }
300:         }
301:     }
302: }

304: impl Rule for PerformanceEngine {
305:     fn id(&self) -> &'static str {
306:         "PERFORMANCE_ENGINE"
307:     }
308: 
309:     fn description(&self) -> &'static str {
310:         "Performance improvement suggestions"
311:     }
312: 
313:     fn severity(&self) -> Severity {
314:         Severity::Info
315:     }
316: 
317:     fn category(&self) -> Category {
318:         Category::Performance
319:     }
320: 
321:     fn target_node_types(&self) -> &'static [&'static str] {
322:         TARGET_NODES
323:     }
324: 
325:     fn has_file_check(&self) -> bool {
326:         true
327:     }
328: 
329:     fn check(&self, ctx: &NodeContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
330:         match ctx.node.kind() {
331:             "function_call" => self.check_function_call(ctx.node, ctx.source),
332:             "command" => self.check_command(ctx.node, ctx.source),
333:             "binary_operator" => {
334:                 let mut diags = self.check_binary_operator(ctx.node, ctx.source);
335:                 // Also check for AND2/OR2 (& and | parse as binary_operator).
336:                 diags.extend(self.check_boolean_context_binary(ctx.node, ctx.source));
337:                 diags
338:             }
339:             "boolean_operator" => {
340:                 // boolean_operator is for && / || which are already correct.
341:                 Vec::new()
342:             }
343:             "comparison_operator" => self.check_comparison(ctx.node, ctx.source),
344:             "unary_operator" => self.check_unary(ctx.node, ctx.source),
345:             _ => Vec::new(),
346:         }
347:     }
348: 
349:     fn check_file(&self, ctx: &FileContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
350:         self.check_growth_in_loops(ctx.tree, ctx.source)
351:     }
352: }

358: pub(crate) fn make_diag(check_id: &'static str, node: tree_sitter::Node) -> Diagnostic {
359:     let start = node.start_position();
360:     Diagnostic {
361:         rule_id: check_id,
362:         message: check_description(check_id).to_string(),
363:         severity: Severity::Info,
364:         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
365:         line: start.row + 1,
366:         column: start.column + 1,
367:         fix: None,
368:     }
369: }
370: pub(crate) fn make_diag_with_fix(
371:     check_id: &'static str,
372:     node: tree_sitter::Node,
373:     fix: Option<Fix>,
374: ) -> Diagnostic {
375:     let start = node.start_position();
376:     Diagnostic {
377:         rule_id: check_id,
378:         message: check_description(check_id).to_string(),
379:         severity: Severity::Info,
380:         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
381:         line: start.row + 1,
382:         column: start.column + 1,
383:         fix,
384:     }
385: }
386: pub(crate) fn node_text<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
387:     &source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()]
388: }
389: pub(crate) fn extract_func_name<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
390:     if node.kind() != "function_call" {
391:         return None;
392:     }
393:     let name_node = node.child_by_field_name("name")?;
394:     Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
395: }
396: pub(crate) fn extract_command_name<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
397:     if node.kind() != "command" {
398:         return None;
399:     }
400:     let name_node = node.child(0)?;
401:     if name_node.kind() == "command_name" {
402:         Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
403:     } else {
404:         None
405:     }
406: }
407: pub(crate) fn extract_command_args<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Vec<&'a str> {
408:     let mut args = Vec::new();
409:     let count = node.child_count();
410:     for i in 0..count {
411:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
412:             // Skip the command_name (first child) and punctuation.
413:             if child.kind() == "command_name" || child.kind() == ";" || child.kind() == "," {
414:                 continue;
415:             }
416:             let text = node_text(child, source).trim();
417:             if !text.is_empty() {
418:                 args.push(text);
419:             }
420:         }
421:     }
422:     args
423: }
424: pub(crate) fn extract_operator<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
425:     // The operator is typically the second child (between left and right operands),
426:     // or we can scan children for the operator token.
427:     let count = node.child_count();
428:     for i in 0..count {
429:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
430:             let text = node_text(child, source);
431:             // Operator tokens are short and not identifiers/expressions.
432:             match text {
433:                 "+" | "-" | "*" | "/" | "\\" | "^" | ".*" | "./" | ".\\" | ".^" | "&" | "|"
434:                 | "&&" | "||" | "==" | "~=" | "<" | ">" | "<=" | ">=" => return text,
435:                 _ => continue,
436:             }
437:         }
438:     }
439:     ""
440: }
441: pub(crate) fn extract_unary_operator<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
442:     if let Some(child) = node.child(0) {
443:         let text = node_text(child, source);
444:         match text {
445:             "~" | "-" | "+" | "!" => return text,
446:             _ => {}
447:         }
448:     }
449:     ""
450: }
451: pub(crate) fn first_named_child(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> Option<tree_sitter::Node> {
452:     let count = node.named_child_count();
453:     if count > 0 {
454:         node.named_child(0)
455:     } else {
456:         None
457:     }
458: }
459: pub(crate) fn count_args(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> usize {
460:     // Arguments are in the `arguments` child node.
461:     match find_arguments(node) {
462:         Some(args_node) => args_node.named_child_count(),
463:         None => 0,
464:     }
465: }
466: pub(crate) fn find_arguments<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) -> Option<tree_sitter::Node<'a>> {
467:     let count = node.child_count();
468:     for i in 0..count {
469:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
470:             if child.kind() == "arguments" {
471:                 return Some(child);
472:             }
473:         }
474:     }
475:     None
476: }
477: pub(crate) fn has_string_arg(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str, value: &str) -> bool {
478:     let count = node.child_count();
479:     for i in 0..count {
480:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
481:             let text = node_text(child, source);
482:             // Match quoted strings: 'value' or "value"
483:             let trimmed = text.trim_matches('\'').trim_matches('"');
484:             if trimmed.eq_ignore_ascii_case(value) {
485:                 return true;
486:             }
487:             // Recurse into arguments node.
488:             if child.kind() == "arguments" && has_string_arg(child, source, value) {
489:                 return true;
490:             }
491:         }
492:     }
493:     false
494: }
495: pub(crate) fn has_exist_type_arg(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
496:     // exist should have 2 arguments, with the second being a string like 'file', 'dir'.
497:     let arg_count = count_args(node);
498:     if arg_count < 2 {
499:         return false;
500:     }
501:     has_string_arg(node, source, "file")
502:         || has_string_arg(node, source, "dir")
503:         || has_string_arg(node, source, "builtin")
504:         || has_string_arg(node, source, "class")
505: }
506: pub(crate) fn has_simple_regex_pattern(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
507:     // Look for the second argument (the pattern) and check if it's purely alphanumeric
508:     // (meaning a simple `contains` or `strcmp` would suffice).
509:     let args_node = match find_arguments(node) {
510:         Some(n) => n,
511:         None => return false,
512:     };
513: 
514:     // The pattern is usually the 2nd argument.
515:     let named_count = args_node.named_child_count();
516:     if named_count < 2 {
517:         return false;
518:     }
519: 
520:     if let Some(pattern_node) = args_node.named_child(1) {
521:         let text = node_text(pattern_node, source);
522:         // Strip quotes.
523:         let inner = text.trim_matches('\'').trim_matches('"');
524:         // If the pattern is purely alphanumeric (no regex metacharacters), it's simple.
525:         if !inner.is_empty() && inner.chars().all(|c| c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '_') {
526:             return true;
527:         }
528:     }
529:     false
530: }
531: pub(crate) fn has_strcmp_arg(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
532:     let args_node = match find_arguments(node) {
533:         Some(n) => n,
534:         None => return false,
535:     };
536: 
537:     if let Some(first_arg) = first_named_child(args_node) {
538:         if first_arg.kind() == "function_call" {
539:             if let Some(name) = extract_func_name(first_arg, source) {
540:                 return name == "strcmp" || name == "strcmpi";
541:             }
542:         }
543:     }
544:     false
545: }
546: pub(crate) fn is_nested_same_call(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str, func_name: &str) -> bool {
547:     let args_node = match find_arguments(node) {
548:         Some(n) => n,
549:         None => return false,
550:     };
551: 
552:     // Check if first argument is a function_call with the same name.
553:     if let Some(first_arg) = first_named_child(args_node) {
554:         if first_arg.kind() == "function_call" {
555:             if let Some(inner_name) = extract_func_name(first_arg, source) {
556:                 return inner_name == func_name;
557:             }
558:         }
559:     }
560:     false
561: }
562: pub(crate) fn is_subscript_context(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
563:     if let Some(parent) = node.parent() {
564:         // Direct parent might be `arguments` of a function_call.
565:         if parent.kind() == "arguments" {
566:             if let Some(grandparent) = parent.parent() {
567:                 return grandparent.kind() == "function_call";
568:             }
569:         }
570:         // Or the parent is directly a function_call (as an argument).
571:         if parent.kind() == "function_call" {
572:             // Make sure this node is not the function name itself.
573:             if let Some(name_node) = parent.child_by_field_name("name") {
574:                 return name_node.id() != node.id();
575:             }
576:         }
577:     }
578:     false
579: }
580: pub(crate) fn is_statement_level(node: &tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
581:     node.parent()
582:         .map(|p| matches!(p.kind(), "source_file" | "block"))
583:         .unwrap_or(false)
584: }
585: pub(crate) fn is_inside_loop(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
586:     let mut current = node.parent();
587:     while let Some(p) = current {
588:         match p.kind() {
589:             "for_statement" | "while_statement" => return true,
590:             "function_definition" => return false, // Stop at function boundary.
591:             _ => {}
592:         }
593:         current = p.parent();
594:     }
595:     false
596: }
597: pub(crate) fn is_in_condition(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
598:     let mut current = node.parent();
599:     while let Some(p) = current {
600:         match p.kind() {
601:             "if_statement" | "while_statement" | "elseif_clause" => {
602:                 // Check if our node is in the condition part, not the body.
603:                 // The condition is typically the first expression child after the keyword.
604:                 if let Some(cond) = p.child_by_field_name("condition") {
605:                     return is_descendant_of(node, cond);
606:                 }
607:                 // Fallback: check if node appears before the "block" child.
608:                 let count = p.child_count();
609:                 for i in 0..count {
610:                     if let Some(child) = p.child(i) {
611:                         if child.kind() == "block" {
612:                             // If node is before the block, it's in the condition.
613:                             return node.start_byte() < child.start_byte();
614:                         }
615:                     }
616:                 }
617:                 return true;
618:             }
619:             "function_definition" => return false,
620:             _ => {}
621:         }
622:         current = p.parent();
623:     }
624:     false
625: }
626: pub(crate) fn is_descendant_of(needle: tree_sitter::Node, haystack: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
627:     needle.start_byte() >= haystack.start_byte() && needle.end_byte() <= haystack.end_byte()
628: }
629: pub(crate) fn has_inv_operand(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
630:     let count = node.child_count();
631:     for i in 0..count {
632:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
633:             if child.kind() == "function_call" {
634:                 if let Some(name) = extract_func_name(child, source) {
635:                     if name == "inv" {
636:                         return true;
637:                     }
638:                 }
639:             }
640:         }
641:     }
642:     false
643: }
644: pub(crate) fn has_same_operands(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
645:     // Typically: child(0) = left, child(1) = op, child(2) = right.
646:     let left = match node.child(0) {
647:         Some(n) => n,
648:         None => return false,
649:     };
650:     let right = match node.child(2) {
651:         Some(n) => n,
652:         None => return false,
653:     };
654:     let left_text = node_text(left, source).trim();
655:     let right_text = node_text(right, source).trim();
656:     !left_text.is_empty() && left_text == right_text
657: }
658: pub(crate) fn contains_end_plus_pattern(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
659:     let text = node_text(node, source);
660:     // Simple textual check: look for "end+1" or "end + 1" within parentheses or braces.
661:     let normalized: String = text.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
662:     normalized.contains("end+1")
663: }
664: pub(crate) fn matrix_contains_var(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str, var_name: &str) -> bool {
665:     // Walk the matrix's children looking for an identifier matching var_name.
666:     let count = node.child_count();
667:     for i in 0..count {
668:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
669:             if child.kind() == "identifier" && node_text(child, source) == var_name {
670:                 return true;
671:             }
672:             // Recurse into rows.
673:             if child.kind() == "row" && matrix_contains_var(child, source, var_name) {
674:                 return true;
675:             }
676:         }
677:     }
678:     false
679: }
680: pub(crate) fn extract_length_comparison<'a>(
681:     node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>,
682:     source: &'a str,
683: ) -> Option<(&'a str, &'a str)> {
684:     // comparison_operator children: left op right
685:     let left = node.child(0)?;
686:     let op_node = node.child(1)?;
687:     let right = node.child(2)?;
688: 
689:     let op = node_text(op_node, source);
690:     if op != "==" {
691:         return None;
692:     }
693: 
694:     // Check if left is a function_call to length/numel/size.
695:     if left.kind() == "function_call" {

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verification for the system_objects.rs → system_objects/ mechanical split.

Checks:
1. Moved method bodies match the original (modulo `pub(crate)` and indentation).
2. Each check ID's `make_diag("ID", ...)` appears exactly once across system_objects/.
3. Dispatch references in mod.rs match the moved methods (and no stale references
   in the NEW files).
4. Moved-test count equals the original test count.
5. Original system_objects.rs is untouched (matches HEAD, no diff).
"""
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/home/watermarkhu/repositories/mlt/crates/mlt_rules/src")
ORIG = ROOT / "system_objects.rs"
DIR = ROOT / "system_objects"

failures = []


def fail(msg):
    failures.append(msg)
    print(f"  FAIL: {msg}")


def ok(msg):
    print(f"  ok: {msg}")


def normalize(text: str) -> str:
    """Strip leading whitespace per line, drop blank lines."""
    lines = []
    for ln in text.splitlines():
        s = ln.strip()
        if not s:
            continue
        lines.append(s)
    return "\n".join(lines)


def find_brace_block(text: str, open_idx: int) -> str:
    """Return text from the `{` at open_idx through its matching `}` (inclusive)."""
    depth = 0
    i = open_idx
    n = len(text)
    while i < n:
        c = text[i]
        if c == "{":
            depth += 1
        elif c == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return text[open_idx:i + 1]
        i += 1
    raise RuntimeError("unbalanced braces")


def extract_fn_body(text: str, fn_name: str) -> str:
    """Extract the body (from `{` after signature to matching `}`) of fn `fn_name`."""
    m = re.search(r"\bfn\s+" + re.escape(fn_name) + r"\b", text)
    if not m:
        raise RuntimeError(f"fn {fn_name} not found")
    open_idx = text.index("{", m.end())
    return find_brace_block(text, open_idx)


def extract_if_with_comments(text: str, anchor: str) -> str:
    """Extract a complete `if` statement plus any contiguous comment lines
    immediately preceding it, starting the search at `anchor`."""
    start = text.index(anchor)
    if_start = text.index("if", start)
    open_idx = text.index("{", if_start)
    block = find_brace_block(text, open_idx)
    block_end = open_idx + len(block)
    # walk back over contiguous comment lines immediately before the `if`
    pos = if_start
    while True:
        prev_nl = text.rfind("\n", 0, pos - 1)
        if prev_nl == -1:
            break
        prev_line = text[prev_nl + 1:pos - 1]
        if prev_line.strip().startswith("//"):
            pos = prev_nl + 1
        else:
            break
    return text[pos:block_end]


print("== 1. Moved method bodies match original ==")
orig = ORIG.read_text()

# 1a. Full-method moves: check_reserved_method_names -> check_sorsrvdnm
#     and check_property_defaults -> check_sodfltval
for orig_name, new_name, new_file in [
    ("check_reserved_method_names", "check_sorsrvdnm", DIR / "check_sorsrvdnm.rs"),
    ("check_property_defaults", "check_sodfltval", DIR / "check_sodfltval.rs"),
]:
    orig_body = extract_fn_body(orig, orig_name)
    new_body = extract_fn_body(new_file.read_text(), new_name)
    if normalize(orig_body) == normalize(new_body):
        ok(f"{orig_name} -> {new_name}: bodies identical (mod indentation)")
    else:
        fail(f"{orig_name} -> {new_name}: bodies DIFFER")

# 1b. Extracted blocks from check_function_call -> check_sonumin/check_sonumout/check_sodeprop
extractions = [
    ("SONUMIN block -> check_sonumin", "// SONUMIN: Check argument count", DIR / "check_sonumin.rs"),
    ("SONUMOUT block -> check_sonumout", "// SONUMOUT: Calling release()/reset()", DIR / "check_sonumout.rs"),
    ("SODEPPROP block -> check_sodeprop", "// SODEPPROP: Detect access to deprecated", DIR / "check_sodeprop.rs"),
]
fc_text = orig[orig.index("fn check_function_call"):]
for label, anchor, new_file in extractions:
    orig_block = extract_if_with_comments(fc_text, anchor)
    new_text = new_file.read_text()
    new_block = extract_if_with_comments(new_text, anchor)
    if normalize(orig_block) == normalize(new_block):
        ok(f"{label}: identical (mod indentation)")
    else:
        fail(f"{label}: DIFFER")

print()
print("== 2. Each check ID's make_diag appears exactly once ==")
check_ids = ["SONUMIN", "SONUMOUT", "SODEPPROP", "SORSRVDNM", "SODFLTVAL"]
all_text = "\n".join(p.read_text() for p in DIR.glob("*.rs"))
for cid in check_ids:
    count = len(re.findall(rf'make_diag\("{cid}"', all_text))
    if count == 1:
        ok(f"{cid}: exactly one make_diag call")
    else:
        fail(f"{cid}: make_diag count = {count}")

mod_rs = (DIR / "mod.rs").read_text()
all_nine = ["SONUMIN", "SONUMOUT", "SODEPPROP", "SOINITPROP", "SODFLTVAL",
            "SORSRVDNM", "SOTUNPROP1", "SOTUNPROP3", "SOTUNPROP4"]
for cid in all_nine:
    if len(re.findall(rf'\b{cid}\b', mod_rs)) >= 1:
        ok(f"{cid} present in mod.rs metadata")
    else:
        fail(f"{cid} missing from mod.rs")

print()
print("== 3. Dispatch references match ==")
for cid, meth in [
    ("SONUMIN", "check_sonumin"),
    ("SONUMOUT", "check_sonumout"),
    ("SODEPPROP", "check_sodeprop"),
    ("SORSRVDNM", "check_sorsrvdnm"),
    ("SODFLTVAL", "check_sodfltval"),
]:
    defs = []
    for p in DIR.glob("check_*.rs"):
        t = p.read_text()
        if re.search(rf"\bfn\s+{meth}\b", t):
            defs.append(p.name)
    if len(defs) == 1:
        ok(f"{meth} defined in {defs[0]}")
    else:
        fail(f"{meth} defined in {len(defs)} files: {defs}")
    refs = len(re.findall(rf"self\.{meth}\(", mod_rs))
    if refs >= 1:
        ok(f"mod.rs dispatches to {meth} ({refs} call site(s))")
    else:
        fail(f"mod.rs does NOT reference {meth}")

# no stale references to old method names in the NEW files (original untouched by design)
stale = []
for p in DIR.glob("*.rs"):
    t = p.read_text()
    for old in ["check_reserved_method_names", "check_property_defaults"]:
        if re.search(rf"\b{old}\b", t):
            stale.append(f"{p.name}: {old}")
if stale:
    fail(f"stale references in new files: {stale}")
else:
    ok("no stale references to old method names in new system_objects/ files")

# new submodule declarations in mod.rs all exist as files
for p in DIR.glob("check_*.rs"):
    name = p.stem
    if re.search(rf"^\s*mod\s+{re.escape(name)};", mod_rs, re.MULTILINE):
        ok(f"mod.rs declares mod {name}")
    else:
        fail(f"mod.rs missing mod {name}")

print()
print("== 4. Test counts ==")
orig_tests = len(re.findall(r"#\[test\]", orig))
moved_tests = sum(len(re.findall(r"#\[test\]", p.read_text())) for p in DIR.glob("check_*.rs"))
mod_tests = len(re.findall(r"#\[test\]", mod_rs))
if orig_tests == moved_tests == 13 and mod_tests == 0:
    ok(f"original {orig_tests} tests == moved {moved_tests} tests; 0 left in mod.rs")
else:
    fail(f"original={orig_tests} moved={moved_tests} mod.rs={mod_tests}")

orig_test_names = re.findall(r"#\[test\]\n\s*fn\s+(\w+)", orig)
new_test_names = re.findall(r"#\[test\]\n\s*fn\s+(\w+)", all_text)
if sorted(orig_test_names) == sorted(new_test_names):
    ok(f"test names preserved: {len(orig_test_names)}")
else:
    missing = set(orig_test_names) - set(new_test_names)
    extra = set(new_test_names) - set(orig_test_names)
    fail(f"test name mismatch; missing={missing} extra={extra}")

print()
print("== 5. Original file untouched ==")
r = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "-C", "/home/watermarkhu/repositories/mlt", "diff", "--stat", "--",
     "crates/mlt_rules/src/system_objects.rs"],
    capture_output=True, text=True,
)
if r.stdout.strip():
    fail(f"system_objects.rs has uncommitted diff:\n{r.stdout}")
else:
    ok("system_objects.rs has no diff (untouched)")

print()
if failures:
    print(f"VERIFICATION FAILED: {len(failures)} issue(s)")
    sys.exit(1)
print("VERIFICATION PASSED")
